summary: GWG is a design-build construction management and consulting firm at 55 Carter Drive, Suite 104 in Edison, NJ, working since 2003 for commercial property owners and developers on retrofits, expansions, owner's representation, property condition assessments and ground-up builds across NJ, NY and PA. Its public footprint shows a firm investing in construction technology (BIM, 3D takeoffs, site cameras, smart kiosks) and in leadership depth, with a CFO and two new VPs appearing on its people page in 2026 while it recruits for project-management roles. Client intake is still phone-and-web-form only, with no online booking, portal, published hours or after-hours channel.

facts.fact: GWG describes itself as a design-build construction management and consulting company based in Edison, NJ, serving commercial property owners and developers; located at 55 Carter Drive #104, Edison, NJ 08817, phone (732) 494-8370.
The firm says its team has supported property owners, developers and operating executives since 2003 across New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

Service lines: property condition assessments, full-scope construction management as general contractor, owner's representation, design/build, and value engineering, organized around a 4-stage lifecycle (initiation, preconstruction, construction, closeout).
Named verticals: commercial properties, light manufacturing, food preparation, sports facilities and warehouse projects.

Portfolio includes 12 published projects such as Sampled SMART Laboratories (Piscataway), Ranney School Library, Iron Peak Sports and Events Center (Hillsborough), Sportika (Manalapan), Simon and Schuster (Delran), Ray Catena Lexus of Monmouth and a PPI warehouse expansion in Edison.
Featured project: a 140,000 sq ft specialty life-sciences cold storage laboratory and biorepository for Sampled SMART Labs.

Leadership page lists Eric Gatti (President | CEO), Nicholas Gorski (EVP), Seth Gross (CFO), Eric Korb (Chief Administrative & Technology Officer), Jeremy Weissman (VP Operations), Jay Stasi (VP Development), Chris Guderian (Project Executive) and Michael Benevento (Lead Estimator); the page was last updated October 2026 and carries 2026 uploads for Gross, Weissman and Stasi headshots.

Eric Korb's role is defined to cover finance, IT, human capital, marketing and business-process optimization; Nicholas Gorski's remit covers project financial controls, preconstruction, estimating, procurement, compliance and development.

GWG was named Edison (NJ) Chamber of Commerce Member of the Year, and the Edison Chamber directory lists GWG under Contractors / Manufacturing & Production with reps Eric Gatti, Brian Keaton, Eric Korb and Rupali Lubchansky.

Published projects cited in company news include selection by The Hampshire Companies as owner's representative for an NJ industrial portfolio, and a fast-tracked conversion of a 21-acre Class B office site to warehouse use.
GWG is an authorized builder for American Buildings Company and holds memberships in NACBI, U.S. Green Building Council, IOREBA and the Material Handling Society of New Jersey.

operations_signals: Inbound is phone plus a website contact form: 'Fill out our contact form below, or feel free to call, and we will contact you to assess your needs and issue a proposal' — no online booking, scheduling widget, client portal or published business hours (https://www.gwgllc.com/contact-us/).

Subcontractor onboarding runs through a separate 'Submit Subcontractor Application Form' link on the contact page, so sub qualification and bid intake are separate manual workflows (https://www.gwgllc.com/contact-us/).

Sales process is consultative and proposal-based, with pre-construction starting from due diligence, feasibility, programming, permitting and bidding/estimating stages (https://www.gwgllc.com/services/).

Project delivery is site-heavy and coordination-heavy: PMs own schedules and must coordinate design team, subcontractors, stakeholders and Site Superintendents from pre-construction handoff to closeout (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/construction-project-manager/).
Service area is New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania, run from one Edison office; hours and after-hours coverage are not published anywhere on the site (https://www.gwgllc.com/about/).

Careers intake is a web 'Apply Now' form with reCAPTCHA and no ATS link visible, meaning applications likely land in an inbox rather than a tracking system (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/construction-project-manager/).
hiring_signals: Two open roles posted on GWG's own careers page: Construction Project Manager (owns schedule creation and drives projects from pre-con handoff through closeout) and Assistant Project Manager (reviews plans and specs, analyzes take-offs, pricing and bidding) (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/).

Careers page states GWG is 'always looking' for candidates in engineering, design, project management, client service and administration, indicating evergreen, high-turnover-adjacent hiring in client service and admin (https://www.gwgllc.com/people/).

Two new executive roles appeared on the people page in 2026 — VP Operations (project launch, resource planning, scope, schedule, budgets, forecasting) and VP Development — alongside a CFO, a sign of formalizing controls as project volume grows (https://www.gwgllc.com/people/).

The Assistant PM posting centers on take-offs, pricing and bid analysis, i.e., the manual estimating/bid-leveling work that typically consumes junior staff hours (https://www.gwgllc.com/career/assistant-project-manager/).
review_themes: No third-party review profile was retrievable: Google Business, Yelp, BBB, Glassdoor, Indeed and ZipRecruiter all blocked automated access, so no independent customer or employee review themes could be verified (sources blocked: bbb.org, glassdoor.com, indeed.com, ziprecruiter.com).

The only customer voice available is GWG's own site testimonials: a warehouse client praises the team as professionals and says it is on its third project with them and would hire again; a second client (Independent Chemical) highlights a cross-functional team spanning regulatory, structural and construction (https://www.gwgllc.com/portfolio/).
Testimonial placement is thin and static — two attributed quotes reused across the portfolio, career and industry pages, with no dates or review-platform links (https://www.gwgllc.com/portfolio/).
tech_footprint: BIM-anchored delivery: 3D architectural models feed quantity takeoffs for estimating, with simulated maintenance and operations scenarios used in financial analysis (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).
Integrated estimating/project-management software that taps a network of vetted vendors and analyzes bids in real time (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).

Field tech: geolocated site cameras for remote visual inspection, 3D cameras plus AI tools measuring progress toward completion, and smart kiosks managing subcontractor attendance and safety compliance (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).
Post-construction building monitoring via sensors tracking HVAC, lighting, electrical and security data points around the clock (https://www.gwgllc.com/services/).
Closeout documentation (daily logs, progress tracking, video recordings, cost breakdowns) is produced from the same integrated system (https://www.gwgllc.com/our-technology/).

Website is WordPress with Yoast SEO and Google reCAPTCHA on forms; social presence spans LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube and Instagram, but no named CRM, ERP, scheduling or client-portal product is disclosed (https://www.gwgllc.com/contact-us/).
Content marketing is stale: the news/blog archive's newest posts date to mid-2023 even though leadership pages were updated in 2026 (https://www.gwgllc.com/gwg-news/).
growth_signals: Executive bench expanded in 2026 with a CFO (Seth Gross), VP Operations (Jeremy Weissman) and VP Development (Jay Stasi), the latter joining after serving as VP of Development at The Hampshire Companies (https://www.gwgllc.com/people/).
Selected as owner's representative for The Hampshire Companies' New Jersey industrial portfolio — a program-level, multi-property mandate rather than a single job (https://www.gwgllc.com/gwg-news/).
Fast-track warehouse conversion work: a redeveloper's 21-acre central NJ site converting under-utilized Class B office space to warehouse use (https://www.gwgllc.com/gwg-news/).

Large-format specialty project wins: 140,000 sq ft life-sciences cold storage lab/biorepository and multiple indoor sports complexes (Iron Peak, Sportika, Florham Park) (https://www.gwgllc.com/portfolio/).
Named Edison Chamber of Commerce Member of the Year, and still listed as an active chamber member in Edison (https://www.edisonchamber.com/members/member/g-william-group-llc-6655).

Trade-association footprint (American Buildings Company authorized builder, IOREBA, NACBI, USGBC, Material Handling Society of NJ) points to continued pursuit of industrial/warehouse work in the NY-NJ-PA corridor (https://www.gwgllc.com/about/).
decision_maker: Eric Gatti, President | CEO — https://www.gwgllc.com/people/ (also listed as the Edison Chamber rep contact at https://www.edisonchamber.com/members/member/g-william-group-llc-6655)

inferences.inference: Estimating and bid leveling are the heaviest manual, spreadsheet-like workload and the best first AI target.
inferences.reasoning: GWG advertises 3D-model takeoffs and real-time bid analysis, and its open Assistant PM role is explicitly about take-offs, pricing and bidding; small firms at this stage typically still stitch those outputs together by hand for each fast-track proposal.

inferences.inference: Inbound lead handling likely depends on a person answering the phone or triaging a web form, creating missed-opportunity risk.
inferences.reasoning: The site offers only a contact form and a phone number, publishes no hours, booking link or after-hours path, and says response is a callback that leads to a proposal — a manual sequence with no automated qualification.

inferences.inference: Project managers are coordination bottlenecks across design team, subs, superintendents and owners.
inferences.reasoning: The PM job posting assigns schedule creation and full-cycle coordination to a single role that hands off from a separate pre-construction team, and VP Operations exists to plan resources and forecast — classic signs of stretched PM capacity.

inferences.inference: Back-office finance and reporting are maturing right now, which makes document/report automation timely.
inferences.reasoning: A CFO and a Chief Administrative & Technology Officer with finance/IT/process remits both sit on the leadership page, and the site advertises closeout packages, daily logs and cost breakdowns as deliverables — all recurring documents.

inferences.inference: Marketing and proposal content is under-maintained, an easy adjacent AI win.
inferences.reasoning: News posts stop in mid-2023 while headshots and bios were refreshed in 2026, and the same two testimonials are recycled across pages.

inferences.inference: The firm is likely small (tens of employees) with a lean back office.
inferences.reasoning: One office, eight named leaders covering executive, estimating and field roles, two open PM-ish roles, and applications taken by web form rather than an ATS; no headcount is published, so size is estimated, not stated.

data_gaps: No independent customer reviews verified — Google Business, Yelp, BBB, Glassdoor, Indeed and ZipRecruiter all returned 403/blocking to automated access, so review themes rest only on the firm's own testimonials.
No job-board postings confirmed; Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor were inaccessible, so hiring signals come only from GWG's own careers page.
Employee headcount, revenue and years-in-business by incorporation date are unconfirmed (LinkedIn company page returned 403; the 'since 2003' claim is the firm's own).
No published business hours, after-hours or emergency coverage, and no named booking/CRM/ERP/portal tools.
No news coverage found in NJBIZ or other regional business press; growth evidence is limited to the firm's own site and the Edison Chamber listing.
Web search providers were rate-limited or unconfigured during this run, so discovery relied on direct fetches of the firm's site and its sitemaps plus the chamber page.
